properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-22, raised at the dev_reflow2 hub (a design over reflow2 and flo2) and deliberately recorded HERE rather than in the hub, because it is a question about how reflow2 behaves.

═══ THE IDEA, IN HIS WORDS ═══
"is a rule the right call? what happens for when my brother sets up a project hub at his work place — does he need to remember to add a rule in his project-brain? I don't like trusting that he remembers and then forgets and has to somehow transcribe whatever design content back to the lower levels. One other potential solution is that within reflow2, we could stipulate that any fact only appears 'once'. Then when reflow2 is used at the hub-level, the agent can see when it runs a skill that facts can only be found once and should be at the lowest level. Then you are relying on the ability of reflow2 to query that fact later on."

═══ WHAT PROMPTED IT ═══
At the hub, the agent proposed a RULE ("an idea goes into the child that would act on it; the hub holds only what no child can hold"). Anthony's objection is to the MECHANISM, not the content: a rule each hub owner has to install and remember is the "a rule written down is not a rule that reaches the moment" failure this design has measured twice (fact:the-authoritative-object-rule-recurred-twelve-days-later-including-two-instances-it-already-listed). He wants the invariant to SHIP IN reflow2, so every hub (Alex's at work included) gets it without anyone remembering.

═══ WHY IT IS SHARPER THAN WHAT IS ALREADY RECORDED ═══
⭐ It answers the copy-vs-reference sub-question in dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs ("a copy is a second source of truth; a reference means the child's graph cannot be read alone"), and it answers it by moving the cost. If a fact lives at the LOWEST level, every child can still be read alone, because its facts are its own. Only the HUB depends on references. A hub is a reader by nature, so that is the right place for the dependency to sit. The objection to references was real for DOWNWARD inheritance (the fact in the hub, the child pointing up) and mostly disappears when the fact lives below and the hub points down.
⭐ It turns hxm_program's observed defect (the hub keeps shadow copies of the sim's capabilities, and nothing flags the duplication: dec:idea-a-hub-owns-designs-it-does-not-absorb-and-that-is-a-third-relation, item 1) from a detector someone must run into an invariant that refuses or warns at write time.

═══ SHAPES IT COULD TAKE (none chosen) ═══
(a) ADVISORY. When a session holds or knows about several related designs, the write guard also searches the sibling and child designs, and says "this already lives in <design>:<node>, so reference it there". Cheapest; reuses the near-duplicate guard and the fan-out search the hub trial proved (0.24 s across two designs).
(b) REFUSE BY DEFAULT, with an explicit override (`distinct_from` extended across designs), the same shape add_capability's hard refusal has within one design.
(c) THE HOME IS COMPUTED, NOT CHOSEN. "Lowest level that owns ALL of the fact": one child if it concerns one child; the hub only when it genuinely spans children (a portfolio-level call such as starting, stopping or merging projects). Skills (brainstorm, root-cause, capture-intent) are then told their target design by that computation, instead of defaulting to whichever server the session names plainest. Measured at the hub on 2026-09-22: the commands name no design, and with three connected the default is the hub's own.
(d) A REFERENCE IS A FIRST-CLASS THING. "graph X, node Y" as a typed pointer that resolves and is checked, replacing the prose pointers the hub trial had to write (e.g. flo2's dec:flo2-checks-its-own-stored-files-and-reports-the-result-to-reflow2 names its reflow2 evidence only in text).

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══
🛑 "LOWEST LEVEL" IS NOT ALWAYS ONE PLACE. A manager's cross-cutting decision ("every project authenticates at the gateway") concerns several children at once. Its lowest owning level is the hub. So the invariant does not abolish hub content; it DEFINES it. The hub holds exactly the facts that span children, and nothing a child could hold. That is a feature (it gives the hub a precise job) but it means "the hub holds no design" was never quite the right rule.
🛑 SAME FACT OR MERELY SIMILAR? Enforcing "once" needs to know when two nodes state the same fact, and within ONE design that judgement is already noisy (fact:the-near-match-guard-shows-three-of-a-nine-way-tie-so-relevance-is-decided-by-score-noise). Across designs with different vocabularies it is harder: the hub trial measured flo2 saying "collaborators" and "sessions" where reflow2 says "seats" and "claims". A refusing version (b) would misfire; an advisory version (a) is the honest ceiling until matching improves.
🛑 SANCTIONED COPIES ALREADY EXIST. mirror_surface keeps a pinned copy of another design's published surface on purpose; flo2 holds one of reflow2 today. So the invariant has to read "one HOME, and every other appearance is a DECLARED reference or a DECLARED, dated mirror of it", not literally "appears once". Silent copies are the target, not declared ones.
⚠️ REFERENCE MEANS THE HUB NEEDS THE CHILD TO BE REACHABLE. "Rely on reflow2's ability to query the fact later" is a trade: consistency for availability. If a child's server is down, unexported, or on someone else's machine, the hub knows nothing. hxm_program measured zero of seven siblings exporting (O-02). The hub trial found a running child server started without write-through export, so the hub's own writes sat unexported until done by hand. A copy would have survived either; a reference does not.
⚠️ ENFORCEMENT NEEDS TO KNOW THE FAMILY. A single design cannot check "is this already in a sibling?" unless something says which designs are its siblings. That is the hub's roster, or a registry root, or a declared parent: exactly the "child" relation the hub trial found reflow2 does not have.

═══ SIZE, as a finding not a ranking ═══
(a) is small: an extra search in the write path when a family is known. (c) is medium; most of its value is the skill-targeting half, which is useful on its own. (d) is the expensive one and overlaps dec:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path. (b) should wait for (a)'s false-positive rate to be measured.

═══ GATING ═══
dec:the-hub-waits-for-somebody-to-ask-for-it (accepted 2026-08-29) defers building any of the hub thread until "Alex, or another real user, saying they need it". This brainstorm does not override that. Whether the trigger has now fired (Alex running a work hub; Anthony running dev_reflow2 as a live trial with a written log) is Anthony's call and is not decided here.
properties.name: SETTLED — promoted into: When a session holds several designs, a skill that writes goes to the design the fact belongs in, and says which, instead of defaulting to one (and 1 more)
properties.rationale: Recorded in reflow2's design, not the hub's, applying the idea to itself: it concerns how reflow2 behaves, so reflow2 is its lowest owning level. Searched first with four read-path queries (single source of truth; parent/hub holds nothing; nested graphs; intent crosses designs). The nearest were the three hub-thread ideas and the accepted deferral, all read in full before writing. The write guard then named two of them; both were judged DISTINCT: dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs asks WHAT MAY CROSS a boundary, and dec:idea-the-hub-holds-a-copy-per-sub-repo-and-copies-go-stale asks how a copy stays CURRENT. This proposes an INVARIANT about where any fact lives and who enforces it, which answers a sub-question of the first and removes the premise of the second.
